sentences.text: Case of the claimant 3.

It is the case of the claimant that on 15.07.2023, the claimant along with his father Vishwanath Choudhary were going on bike bearing registration No. HR-24M-0529 to their house at Najafgarh,
Delhi.

When they reached at Parade Road, near St. Mary School, Jharera Cut, the offending vehicle bearing registration No. HR-55AM-6118, which was being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner, hit their bike from left side due to which they fell down and sustained injuries.
It is further stated that the claimant was taken to AHRR Hospital, Delhi Cantt., where his MLC was prepared by the doctors.
Case of respondent no. 1 & 2 4.
Respondents no. 1 and 2 filed their written statement to the DAR wherein it is stated that respondent no. 1 was following traffic rules and regulations which is evident from the CCTV footage.
It is further stated that the complainant Channu Kumar was himself at fault and all other allegations made in the FIR are false and frivolous.

It is further stated that the respondent no. 1 was holding a valid driving license and the alleged offending vehicle was duly insured with respondent no. 3 on the date of accident.
Case of respondent no. 3 5.

Respondent no. 3/Insurance Company filed its legal offer for a sum of Rs.10,000/- for settlement,
which was not accepted by the claimant.
Issues 6.

On 19.11.2024, the following issues were framed by this Tribunal :-
1.

Whether the claimant suffered injuries in a vehicular accident that took place on 18.07.2023 at about 11:15 hrs at Parade Road, Near St. Mary School, Delhi Cantt.,
Delhi involving a vehicle bearing registration No. HR-55AM-6118 (offending vehicle)
being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with R-3/Insurance Company ?

OPP. 
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
3. Relief.

Findings 11.
I have heard arguments and have carefully perused the entire case record.
12. The findings on the aforementioned issues are rendered hereinafter in the succeeding paragraphs.

ISSUE NO. 1 - Whether the claimant suffered injuries in a vehicular accident that took place on 18.07.2023 at about 11:15 hrs at Parade Road, Near St. Mary School, Delhi Cantt., Delhi involving a vehicle bearing registration No. HR-55AM-6118 (offending vehicle) being driven by respondent no. 1 in a rash and negligent manner, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with R-3/Insurance Company ? OPP.
13.
Onus to prove this issue was upon the claimant.

During the course of final arguments, Ld.
Counsels for claimant and respondents have submitted that the issue no. 1 need not be decided since it is not in dispute that the claimant suffered simple injuries due to the accident caused by rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing No. HR-55AM-6118 by respondent no. 1, owned by respondent no. 2 and insured with respondent no. 3 and only the issue no. 2 has to be decided as the quantum of compensation is in dispute.
14. Accordingly, the issue no. 1 need not be decided in the present matter.
ISSUE NO. 2 - Whether the claimant is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?

OPP. 
15.

As the issue No.1 has been decided in favour of the claimant, he has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered by him in the accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
16. In terms of Section 168 of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, the compensation which is to be awarded by this Tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In injury cases, a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensation i.e. pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343, has laid down heads under which Chhannu Kumar Chaudhary vs Dimpy Singh (Magma Insurance) on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126959079/
4 compensation is awarded in personal injury cases as:-
Pecuniary damages (Special Damages)

(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation,

(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising :
(a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment;
(b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability.
(iii) Future medical expenses.
Non-pecuniary damages (General Damages)
(iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

17.

Having considered the ratio of aforesaid judgment, the compensation payable to claimant is assessed hereinafter under the following heads as:-
(i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 18.
Claimant has tendered on record his MLC issued by Army Hospital (R & R) as Ex. PW1/6, the doctor had opined the nature of injuries to be simple.

19. Claimant has also tendered on record his MRI report as Ex. PW1/8 (OSR) in which impression was given to the effect "Disc Osteophyte complex at C-5-6 without neural compromise".
20.
Further, as per medical prescriptions of claimant identified as Ex. PW1/7, the claimant suffered from head ache after the accident for a substantial long period.
21. Claimant has not tendered on record his medical bills pertaining to the injuries sustained in the accident.
Since no medical bills were placed on record by the claimant, he is held not entitled to any amount under this head.
(ii) Loss of earnings 22.
Claimant in his affidavit Ex. PW1/A deposed that he was working as Sergeant at Indian Air Force and was earning a sum of Rs.90,000/- per month.

He has tendered on record copy of his pay slip as Chhannu Kumar Chaudhary vs Dimpy Singh (Magma Insurance) on 30 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126959079/
5 Ex. PW1/4 (OSR), as per which the gross salary of claimant was Rs.90,123/- per month and income tax to the tune of Rs.6,666/- was deducted.

23. In view of the settled law on subject, the tax liability, if any, is to be reduced from his above annual earnings as his 'income' means the actual income less the tax paid, as was also approved in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors., (2017) 16 SCC 680.

After deducting the tax amount of Rs.6,666/-, the salary of claimant comes out to be Rs.83,457/-
per month (Rs.90,123/- - Rs.6,666/-).

Accordingly, the salary of claimant is taken as Rs.83,457/-
per month.
25. Claimant in his affidavit further deposed that he had taken leave for a period of 19 days after the accident.
He has tendered on record copy of his leave certificate as Ex. PW1/5 (OSR), as per which he was on leave from 18.07.2023 to 05.08.2023, i.e. for a period of 19 days.
26. It is explicit from the testimony of claimant coupled with exhibited document that the claimant had availed leaves for a total period of 19 days due to the injuries sustained in the accident.

27. In terms of the judgment dated 04.09.2012 given by the Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case of Sandeep Mishra Vs. Ajay Kumar Yadav & Ors., MAC App. No.215/2010, the petitioner is entitled to be compensated for all those leaves availed by him due to above accident irrespective of the nature of these leaves as it is now well settled that even if the leaves were paid leaves, the petitioner is entitled to be reimbursed for the same as he could have enjoyed or availed his leaves later on for his enjoyment or for enjoyment of his family members.

sentences.text: 28. In view of aforesaid Judgment, this Tribunal feels it just and reasonable to compensate him for loss of earning equivalent to a period of 19 days.
Therefore, under this head, he is being awarded an amount of Rs.52,856/- (rounded off) (Rs.83,457/30 X 19 days).
(iii) Mental and Physical Shock, Pain and Sufferings & Loss of Amenities 29.
As stated above, the claimant had suffered simple injuries in the accident.
However, as per medical prescriptions of claimant identified as Ex. PW1/7, the claimant suffered from head ache after the accident for a substantial long period.
He also had difficulty in sleeping and had worrying thoughts.
He also underwent MRI of the brain which is usually advised in cases of serious injuries.

30. Though it is not possible to exactly compensate him for the shock, pain and sufferings etc. which he had actually suffered because of the above injuries, but an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by the claimant and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.25,000/- each is being awarded to him towards (i) mental and physical shock and (ii) for pain and sufferings respectively, as claimed in the written submissions filed on behalf of claimant.
However, no amount is being awarded to the claimant towards loss of amenities.
Thus, he is awarded total amount of Rs.50,000/- under this head.

sentences.text: The claimant in his affidavit deposed that he had spent a sum of Rs.400/- per day for a period of three months towards special diet and Rs.30,000/- on conveyance.
However, he has not placed on record any document in order to substantiate his above claim.

Still this Tribunal can very well take note of the requirement of conveyance for claimant for visiting the hospitals and doctors in connection with his treatment and special diet for his early recovery from the injuries suffered because of the accident.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the present case, an amount of Rs.10,000/- each is being awarded to the claimant towards conveyance and special diet.

32. The claimant in his affidavit deposed that he had hired an attendant for a period of 20 days @
Rs.18,000/- per month.

Keeping in view the nature of injuries suffered by the claimant, he would have required assistance of some family member/attendant for doing his daily routine work for a period of 20 days, therefore, an amount of Rs.12,000/- for 20 days @ Rs.18,000/- is also being awarded to the claimant towards attendant charges.
The claimant is thus entitled to an amount of Rs.32,000/- (Rs.10,000/- + Rs.10,000 + Rs. 12,000/-) under this head.
ISSUE No. 3/Relief 33.

In view of foregoing discussion, the claimant is thus awarded a sum of Rs.1,34,856/- (Rupees One Lakh Thirty Four Thousand Eight Hundred Fifty Six only) (Rs.52,856/- + Rs.50,000/- +
Rs.32,000/-) along with 7.5% interest from the date of filing of DAR.
However, it is directed that the amount of interim award and interest for the suspended period, if any, during the course of this inquiry, shall be liable to be excluded from the award amount.
RELEASE 34.
The entire awarded amount is directed to be released in the saving bank account of claimant through RTGS/NEFT or any other electronic mode.
LIABILITY 35.

All the respondents are though being held jointly and severally liable to pay the awarded amount of compensation to petitioners, but respondent no.3 being insurer of offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the award amount with UCO Bank, Patiala House Court Branch, along with interest @ 7.5%
per annum from the date of filing of DAR by RTGS/NEFT/IMPS in bank account being maintained in the above said bank in name of this tribunal within 30 days from today, failing which it is liable to pay interest at the rate of 9% per annum for the period of delay.

In case even after lapse of 90 days from today, respondent no. 3 fails to deposit this compensation with interest, in that event, in light of judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi passed in the case of New India Assurance Company Limited Vs. Kashmiri Lal 2007 ACJ 688 , this compensation shall be recovered by attaching the bank account of respondent no. 3 with a cost of Rs.5,000/-.
